lede: People of scripture and people of idols alike had been waiting, each in their own way, for something to settle the matter. It came: a Messenger from Allah, reciting pages kept pure. This surah is about what they did next.

names.name: al-Bayyinah
names.note: After the word that ends its first ayah: they were not going to leave what they were upon until the clear proof came to them.

names.name: Lam Yakun
names.note: Its opening words, and the name it has in the hadith: the Prophet ﷺ told Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, “Allah has commanded me to recite to you ‘Lam yakuni lladhīna kafarū’” (al-Bukhārī 4959). Al-Qurṭubī heads it with this name.

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī gives the view that it is Madinan as that of the majority, and al-Qurṭubī attributes it to Ibn ʿAbbās and most of the scholars. That it is Makkan is reported by Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās and was the choice of Yaḥyā ibn Sallām. Its subject favours Madinah: it addresses the People of the Book first and the idolaters second, and speaks of prayer and zakāh together as the upright religion.
revelation.when: Madinah, where the message was now being put to Jews and Christians as well as to the Arabs

evidence.quote: وَفِيها قَوْلانِ أحَدُهُما: مَدَنِيَّةٌ، قالَهُ الجُمْهُورُ. والثّانِي: مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَهُ أبُو صالِحٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، واخْتارَهُ يَحْيى بْنُ سَلامٍ
وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ يَحْيَى بْنُ سَلَّامٍ. وَمَدَنِيَّةٌ، فِي قَوْلِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَالْجُمْهُورِ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ﴾ بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Madinah. Recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.

attested.quote: هي مَدَنِيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ الجُمْهُورِ، وقِيلَ مَكِّيَّةٌ
attested.says: Madinan, in the saying of the majority; a saying that it is Makkan is also mentioned.

setting: In Makkah the argument had been with people who had no scripture. In Madinah the Prophet ﷺ lived beside people who did: the Jewish tribes of the oasis, who had been telling their Arab neighbours for years that a prophet was about to appear, and Christians who came to him from Najrān and elsewhere.

This surah speaks to that meeting. Both groups, it says, would not have been parted from their state until a clear proof reached them — and the proof is described exactly: a Messenger from Allah, reciting purified pages in which are upright writings. And yet those who had been given scripture did not split among themselves until after it had come. What they were being asked for was nothing new. It was what they had been commanded from the start: to worship Allah, making the religion His alone, to keep up the prayer and to give the zakāh.
aim: To set out the standing of the Messenger’s ﷺ message — its clarity and its completeness.
themes: The best and worst of creation

outline.title: The proof
outline.summary: Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the idolaters were not going to leave off until the clear proof came to them: a Messenger from Allah, reciting pages made pure, containing writings that are upright.

outline.title: What they did, and what they were asked
outline.summary: Those given the scripture did not divide until after the proof had come to them. Yet they were commanded only this: to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, inclining to the truth, to establish the prayer and to give the zakāh — and that is the religion of uprightness (98:5).

outline.title: Two ends
outline.summary: Those who disbelieve, of the People of the Book and the idolaters, are in the fire of Hell for ever: they are the worst of creatures. Those who believe and do right are the best of creatures: their reward with their Lord is gardens of lasting stay — Allah pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord.

keyAyah.why: The whole of what was asked, in one sentence: sincere worship, prayer, zakāh.

virtues.text: The Prophet ﷺ said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: “Allah has commanded me to recite to you ‘Lam yakuni lladhīna kafarū’.” Ubayy said: “And did He name me?” He said: “Yes.” And Ubayy wept.

before: Al-Qadr told of the night the Book was sent down. Al-Bayyinah tells of the one who brought it, and of how those it reached divided over him.
after: This surah ends on the reward of those who fear their Lord. Al-Zalzalah shows the Day on which that reward is weighed, down to an atom’s weight.

notable.label: Commanded only to worship Allah sincerely
Allah pleased with them, and they with Him
